clue.text: Man's mostly read the Evening Star

parts.note: 'Man's' is short for 'he is', written as one word without the apostrophe

indicators.note: mostly means the synonym loses its final letter, keeping most of it

parts.note: to read carefully is to peruse

explanation.surface: A man reading most of an evening newspaper called the Evening Star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man's' is not a possessive but 'he's'. 'mostly' drops the last E of PERUSE, leaving PERUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesperus is the classical name for the planet Venus seen in the west after sunset.

clue.text: Store heard to be failing, so bargain shrewdly

indicators.note: a store that is failing is falling apart, so these letters break up and reform

explanation.surface: A shop said to be going under, so the owner haggles hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To horse-trade is to negotiate hard and cannily, as dealers once haggled over horses.

clue.text: Deceived, as aspiring ventriloquist may be?

definitions.meaning: fooled by a feint, as in rugby where a player fakes a pass
a would-be ventriloquist literally needs to have bought a puppet from a shop

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: someone wanting to take up ventriloquism would have to be supplied with a doll.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sold a dummy is a sporting idiom for being tricked by a fake pass, hence fooled.

clue.text: Highly praise former singer that's not old

parts.note: ex- is the usual prefix for former

indicators.note: not signals that the letter for old is left out of the singer

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice

explanation.surface: Lavishing praise on a one-time vocalist who is still young.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to extol them, raising them high in esteem.

clue.text: Dangerous opponent, no beauty at the checkout

definitions.meaning: a person who is tough and threatening to deal with
literally, an unattractive shopper paying at the till

explanation.definitionFit: An ugly customer is an idiom for a formidable or nasty adversary; read literally it is an unlovely shopper.

clue.text: Has lantern, keeping at an angle

indicators.note: the words hold the answer within them, keeping it inside their letters

explanation.surface: Someone carries a lantern tilted to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant means slanting or obliquely, lying across at an oblique tilt.

clue.text: Represents frosts and winds

indicators.note: winds is a verb here, twisting the letters round into a new order

explanation.surface: A weather symbol that indicates frosts and winds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' reads as a weather noun but is the verb, rhyming with 'finds', signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: If a symbol stands for something it represents or signifies it.

clue.text: A team's pivot

parts.note: a team of eleven is XI in Roman numerals, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: One side's key player around whom everything turns.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is the line or centre about which something rotates, a pivot.

clue.text: Obsessive hauled up a big fish

indicators.note: in a down entry, hauled up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nut is an obsessive enthusiast, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: A fanatical angler lands a huge fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna are large ocean fish, some species growing to several hundred kilograms.

clue.text: Soldiers, responsible and trustworthy

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
liable means legally responsible

explanation.surface: Troops who are accountable and dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliable and trustworthy are synonyms: both mean dependable.

clue.text: To get straight after money is evil

indicators.note: after puts the phrase for straightening behind the abbreviation for money

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for money, as in M1 and M2 measures
to align is to set in a straight line

explanation.surface: The proverb that the love of money is the root of all evil, with a fix-it twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Malign as an adjective means harmful or malevolent, a synonym of wicked.

clue.text: Hard work all for nothing?

parts.note: toil done for no pay, with love meaning nil as in a tennis score

explanation.walkthrough: 'For nothing' suggests futility, but the phrase means unpaid work done out of affection; 'love' is also tennis for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A labour of love is a task undertaken for pleasure or devotion rather than reward.

clue.text: It may bind a sheaf, but it's balanced awkwardly

indicators.note: something placed awkwardly is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sheaf of corn held by something precariously positioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber loop is used to hold together a bundle, such as a sheaf of papers.

clue.text: Why are there boxes on the bridge table? Ominous

definitions.text: Why are there boxes on the bridge table?
definitions.meaning: in tournament bridge, players use boxes of cards to make their calls, so the boxes are there to make calls in the auction

explanation.walkthrough: The first part is answered by splitting the word as 'for bidding': bidding boxes hold the cards used to make calls in the auction at bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbidding means grim and unfriendly-looking, threatening trouble.

clue.text: Splendid get-up to show off

parts.note: grand means impressive or magnificent
to stand is to get up on one's feet

explanation.surface: A dazzling outfit worn to flaunt oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get-up' looks like a noun meaning outfit; it is the verb 'get up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To grandstand is to behave showily to attract applause, like playing to the stands.

clue.text: Plump bird that is widely distributed

definitions.note: the definition describes the thing rather than naming it: a letter or notice circulated among many

parts.note: round means chubby or plump
the robin is a familiar garden bird

explanation.surface: A plump bird, such as a robin, found all over the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin is a letter or petition sent round to many recipients.

clue.text: Make a play of remarkably smart idea

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something unusual done to the words, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever notion is turned into a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: To dramatise a story is to adapt it for performance on stage or screen.

clue.text: Workers, one under purchaser's feet

definitions.meaning: the ordinary employees of a factory, as opposed to management
literally, the surface a customer stands on in a store

explanation.definitionFit: The shop floor is the factory workforce collectively, and literally the floor of a retail store.

clue.text: Belittle Guardian's conduct

parts.note: to demean is to lower someone's dignity
the clue is printed in the Guardian, so the paper's own word for its possession is our

explanation.surface: Disparaging the newspaper's behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often have the publication refer to itself: 'Guardian's' is 'our'.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeanour is outward behaviour or bearing, the way a person conducts themselves.

clue.text: See 15
Criminal oaf's escaped, one in a dark suit

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A lawbreaking lout has broken out, a fugitive in a dark suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in a dark suit' suggests a man in clothes; the suit is spades, a black suit of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The ace is one card, the single pip, in spades, one of the two black suits in a pack.

clue.text: Steadily works gripping tool with no resistance

indicators.note: with no means the letter for resistance is removed

parts.note: pliers are a hand tool for gripping
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A worker plugs away, holding an implement without meeting opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ply a trade is to work at it diligently, so plies means works steadily at.

clue.text: Hurried departure from bed? Nonsense

definitions.meaning: in British slang, to do a ... is to run away suddenly
a narrow bed, often one of a stacked pair
rubbish or claptrap, short for bunkum

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions joined by 'from': 'do a bunk' is British slang for fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a quick getaway, a berth-style bed, and rubbish talk.

clue.text: Spy from Smolensk?

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the city name

explanation.surface: An agent sent from a Russian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a long-term undercover agent inside an organisation.

clue.text: Ideal place, you said, with lots of trimmed bushes

indicators.note: said means the word you is spoken, giving a single letter of the same sound

parts.note: you sounds like the letter U

indicators.note: lots of means most of the synonym is kept, its end cut off

parts.note: topiary is shrubs clipped into ornamental shapes

explanation.surface: A dream garden full of neatly clipped shrubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots of' keeps most of TOPIARY, dropping RY to leave TOPIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is Thomas More's imagined perfect society, hence any perfect place.

clue.text: After party, skirt can almost land in the Caribbean

indicators.note: After puts the skirt and the shortened can behind the party

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a mini is a short skirt

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: After a party, someone in a short skirt might just about reach a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominica is an island nation in the Lesser Antilles in the eastern Caribbean.

clue.text: Goalie for manager

definitions.meaning: the player who guards the goal
someone in charge of something, as a zookeeper or shopkeeper

explanation.definitionFit: A keeper guards the net in football and also looks after or runs something, like a shop.

clue.text: Texted in confusion, no longer young

parts.note: a mess is a state of disorder
aged means old

explanation.surface: An elderly person sending muddled phone messages.
explanation.definitionFit: To have messaged someone is to have sent them a text on a phone.
